question: In Table 2, which passive-targeting delivery systems have a particle size of 150 nm or more, and which of them is the largest?
expect: the PLGA/PLA/PCL polymer system (~180 nm), sEVs (~150 nm), MOF@EVs (~168 nm) and MOF (~485 nm, the largest); passive targeting covers the rows down to GO (active targeting)
rendered:
According to Table 2, the passive-targeting delivery systems with a particle size of 150 nm or more are:

* si-FOXM1-LNPs (particle size: 180 nm)
* siG12D-LODER (particle size: ~141 nm is not 150 nm or more, so this is not included)
* siSnail2-CNP@siSnail2 (particle size: 78.82 ± 11.85 nm is less than 150 nm, so this is not included)
* siTEAD4-MOF@EVs (particle size: ~60 nm is less than 150 nm, so this is not included)
* siSnail-DOX (particle size: 137.4 nm)
* siLPCAT1-CL (particle size: 110 nm is less than 150 nm, so this is not included)
* siM3-PPB@siM3 (particle size: 100 ± 10 nm is less than 150 nm, so this is not included)
* siEGFR-siRNA- AuNP (particle size: 168 nm)
* siCD73- CQD@RM-FA (particle size: ~200 nm)

The largest particle size among these is ~200 nm, which is the particle size of siCD73- CQD@RM-FA.
